title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo

primary.title: Scalable Monte Carlo for Bayesian Learning
primary.anchor: Chapters 1–6; arXiv preprint, 2024 (separate from published book pagination)

scope: Method-family perspective spanning continuous, finite and augmented states. Not a superset of every sampling theorem.

chapters.title: Background

sections.title: Monte Carlo Integration and Bayesian Statistics
Kernels in a Finite-Dimensional Inner Product Space
A New Inner Product and the Kernel Trick in Finite Dimensions
The Power of the Kernel Trick

chapters.motivation: Separate the sampler from its target and its estimator.
chapters.boundary: Share measurable kernels, invariance, covariance and integrability. The RKHS kernel of §1.5 is not a Markov transition kernel. Pull §1.3 forward; stochastic calculus is only a prerequisite for the diffusion branch. A Markov law contract is not an existence theorem for a process or semigroup.

chapters.title: Reversible MCMC and its Scaling
chapters.motivation: Proposals, invariant kernels, and scaling are different obligations.
chapters.boundary: First prove a correctly normalized Metropolis construction, including rejection mass, support and zero-denominator rules. Gibbs/heat-bath updates use a conditional-law adapter. Random-scan mixtures and deterministic-scan compositions have different reversibility properties. Scaling limits are asymptotic claims, not finite-dimensional guarantees.

chapters.title: Stochastic Gradient MCMC Algorithms

sections.title: Controlling Stochasticity in the Gradient Estimator
Example: The Value of Control Variates
Convergence Results for Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics
A General Framework for stochastic gradient MCMC
Guidance for Efficient Scalable Bayesian Learning
Experiments on a Logistic Regression Model
Experiments on a Bayesian Neural Network Model
Scalable Inference for Models in Constrained Spaces
Scalable Inference with Time Series Data

chapters.motivation: An approximate transition need not preserve the intended target.
chapters.boundary: Use a stated time convention: this display is ASTIS normalization, not a verbatim equation of the book. Share the ULA recurrence with the Chewi route through a factor-of-two adapter. Fixed-step ULA/SGLD may have invariant-law bias; drift, stochastic-gradient error, discretization and mixing require separate bounds.

chapters.title: Non-Reversible MCMC
chapters.motivation: Preserving a law is weaker than being reversible.
chapters.boundary: Keep invariance independent of detailed balance. Lifting changes the state, and a marginal target must be proved by projection. Ordinary position-space HMC with the usual symmetrization can be reversible; Hamiltonian dynamics alone is not a blanket nonreversibility certificate. Acceleration depends on an explicit comparator and cost.

chapters.title: Continuous-Time MCMC

sections.title: Continuous-Time MCMC as the Limit of Non-Reversible MCMC
The Generator and Invariant Distribution of a PDMP
The Limiting Process of Section 5.1 as a PDMP

chapters.motivation: A continuous-time method need not be a diffusion.
chapters.boundary: PDMPs combine deterministic flows and jumps. Audit event rates, simulation, non-explosion, generator domains and invariant integration. An infinitesimal balance identity does not by itself construct an invariant Markov semigroup. Continuous time and continuous state are independent axes.

chapters.title: Assessing and Improving MCMC

sections.title: Improved Bias Diagnostics via the Kernel Trick

chapters.motivation: Sampling error, estimator variance and diagnostics are distinct.
chapters.boundary: The covariance series needs stationary sampling and summability; a CLT needs its own assumptions. Diagnostics are not automatic finite-sample certificates. Distinguish Monte Carlo iterations n, data count N and dimension d. Share IPM/transport and covariance tools without treating dependent samples as IID.

extensions.title: General-state convergence: drift, minorisation and coupling
extensions.motivation: Stationarity is only the starting point. Determine from which states the law converges, and whether the rate is qualitative, geometric or uniform.
proof_route: Audit the measurable state and reference measure.
Keep invariance separate from irreducibility and aperiodicity.
Build the small-set coupling from the exact minorisation.
Combine drift and returns to obtain the source-specific bound.
extensions.truth_boundary: Do not infer mixing from detailed balance alone. Preserve exceptional null starting sets, small-set conditions and theorem quantifiers; the displayed conditions are a blueprint, not a complete theorem.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Ergodic averages, Poisson equations and CLTs
extensions.motivation: Estimating an expectation from a dependent path is not the same problem as drawing one nearly stationary sample.
proof_route: Check integrability and centering.
Search shared covariance and L2 interfaces.
Use the source Poisson equation or regeneration route.
Retain variance existence and CLT assumptions explicitly.
extensions.truth_boundary: Do not replace dependent output by IID samples. A small TV error for a marginal law does not prove an estimator CLT or an effective-sample-size formula.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Optimal scaling beyond product targets
extensions.motivation: Separate a high-dimensional optimization criterion from finite-dimensional convergence.
proof_route: Fix the sequence of target laws and proposal scaling.
Audit ESJD and acceptance-limit assumptions.
Check stronger conditions needed for a diffusion limit.
Translate time scaling and cost only through a separate argument.
extensions.truth_boundary: The 0.234 acceptance limit is not a universal tuning theorem. A weak diffusion limit is not by itself a nonasymptotic mixing bound; correlated targets still need the exact source conditions.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Hamiltonian proposals and geometric adapters
extensions.primary_connection: Primary §2.2; geometric comparisons also read Chapter 4.
extensions.motivation: Explain why deterministic numerical trajectories can be used inside an exact-target Markov kernel.
proof_route: Introduce the extended target and momentum law.
Check reversibility/involution and volume or Jacobian conditions.
Apply the acceptance construction on the extended state.
Prove the desired marginal by projection.
extensions.truth_boundary: A Riemannian mass matrix requires determinant/volume and position-dependent corrections. A plain gradient replacement is not Riemannian HMC; no blanket acceleration or nonreversibility claim.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Convex-body MCMC: Hit-and-Run
extensions.primary_connection: Primary §2.1 kernel construction; Vempala §6; cross-link Chewi constrained-sampling topics.
extensions.motivation: The same continuous state space can support a geometric random walk rather than a Langevin proposal.
proof_route: Require a full-dimensional convex body with finite positive volume.
Build a measurable random-direction/chord conditional kernel.
Prove target invariance and required reversibility.
Use isoperimetry/conductance with the source start and oracle model.
extensions.truth_boundary: Uniform on a convex body is log-concave with extended potential, but not a smooth unconstrained potential. Boundary, rounding, warm start and chord-oracle costs remain explicit. Historical survey bounds are not claimed to be current best bounds.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Perturbed kernels: approximation versus exact invariance
extensions.motivation: A cheap transition may approximate an ideal chain while introducing a persistent target bias.
extensions.formula: d(\mu\widetilde P^n,\pi)\le d(\mu\widetilde P^n,\mu P^n)+d(\mu P^n,\pi)
proof_route: State the ideal and implemented kernels separately.
Pin the discrepancy, initialization and local error.
Prove stability/error propagation rather than assume it.
Combine with the ideal mixing bound and report total work.
extensions.truth_boundary: Invariant-law bias need not vanish at a fixed step size. Small local error alone does not give a uniform-in-time bound. General-state drift norms and Wasserstein metrics require separate adapters.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Lifting, bouncy dynamics and PDMP limits
extensions.motivation: Changing the state and clock connects deterministic proposals and event-driven samplers, but not via an unconditional equivalence.
proof_route: Specify the augmented law and its projection.
Audit deterministic flow and jump/refreshment kernels.
State the exact limiting regime.
Only compare efficiency under a fixed observable and cost.
extensions.truth_boundary: Nonreversibility is not uniformly faster. HMC may be reversible at the position-kernel level. A limit theorem is neither equality of finite algorithms nor an identity/composition certificate.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Run length, diagnostics and quantitative guarantees
extensions.motivation: Separate a useful diagnostic from a theorem that controls a stated error.
proof_route: Choose marginal-law error or estimator error.
Record assumptions behind a bound.
Keep diagnostic heuristics labelled.
Separate initialization, iteration count, dimension and data size.
extensions.truth_boundary: A diagnostic threshold alone cannot certify stationarity or a CLT for every target; do not infer an oracle lower bound from a poor chain.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Coupling for unbiased MCMC estimates
extensions.motivation: Use coupling not just to bound mixing, but to construct an unbiased expectation estimator.
proof_route: Build a coupling with correct marginals.
State meeting and faithful-sticking requirements.
Prove telescoping and justify exchanging expectation and series.
Prove finite moments and expected cost separately.
extensions.truth_boundary: An unbiased estimator is not an exact independent sample from the target. Almost-sure meeting alone does not ensure finite variance or finite expected work.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.

extensions.title: Control variates and expectation-preserving corrections
extensions.motivation: Reuse zero-mean identities while keeping a fitted correction distinct from a target-preserving transition.
proof_route: Audit integrability and a genuine zero-mean identity.
Compare stationary asymptotic variance, not just pointwise variance.
Check training and evaluation dependence.
Preserve any boundary terms in generator/Stein identities.
extensions.truth_boundary: Variance reduction is not automatically guaranteed by a zero mean. A fitted correction can introduce bias; a formal generator identity requires its domain and integration-by-parts assumptions.
extensions.attribution: ASTIS extended material, not a chapter of Fearnhead–Nemeth–Oates–Sherlock. No Lean closure asserted.
